cohort: The study analyzed data from 203,990 pregnancies in the Consortium for Safe Labor (2002-2008) dataset, with 1.6% of these complicated by placental abruption.
finding: Placental abruption increased the total risk of perinatal mortality by a factor of 5.4, with both clinician-initiated preterm delivery (< 37 weeks) and spontaneous preterm delivery (< 37 weeks) each mediating approximately 25% of this effect.
